Top 3 Root Causes by Frequency** Below are the three error‑classes that dominate the ~50 K‑line slice, ranked by approximate occurrence: --- ### 1. “Telegram Polling Stall” **Count/Percentage** - ≈ 600 events (∼ 30 % of total error lines) **Evidence (sample lines)** ``` 2026-03-09T02:12:00.448Z [telegram] Polling stall detected (no getUpdates for 894.31s); forcing restart. 2026-03-09T03:14:22.887-07:00 [telegram] Polling stall detected (no getUpdates for 928.28s); forcing restart. 2026-03-10T01:11:22.368-07:00 [telegram] Polling stall detected (no getUpdates for 987.96s); forcing restart. 2026-03-11T15:25:47.229-07:00 [telegram] Polling stall detected (no getUpdates for 962.94s); forcing restart. ``` *(Lines ~1200–~2400 in the log slice.)* **Likely Root Cause** The Telegram long‑poll (“getUpdates”) loop is regularly hanging—no data arrives for many minutes—which triggers the client’s built‑in “stall” detector and restarts the polling. This points at intermittent network/connectivity issues or the bot being overwhelmed so it stops processing updates. --- ### 2. “Telegram API Method Failures” **Count/Percentage** - ≈ 400 events (∼ 20 % of total) **Evidence (sample lines)** **a) Network‐level failures** ``` 2026-03-07T11:31:53.737Z [telegram] deleteWebhook failed: Network request for 'deleteWebhook' failed! 2026-03-07T11:31:54.243Z [telegram] command sync failed: HttpError: Network request for 'setMyCommands' failed! ``` *(Lines ~10–20 in the log slice.)* **b) 404 “Not Found” failures** ``` 2026-03-07T11:37:07.707Z [telegram] deleteWebhook failed: Call to 'deleteWebhook' failed! (404: Not Found) 2026-03-07T11:37:08.195Z [telegram] command sync failed: GrammyError: Call to 'setMyCommands' failed! (404: Not Found) ``` *(Lines ~60–80.)* **c) sendMessage Bad Requests** ``` 2026-03-08T11:28:13.487Z [telegram] message failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: message to be replied not found) ``` *(Lines ~270 in the log slice.)* **Likely Root Cause** The gateway’s Telegram‑related API calls are repeatedly failing—in two distinct modes: (1) transient network timeouts and DNS/HTTP errors, (2) 404/400 errors indicating invalid or stale webhook/command state (e.g. deleting an already‑deleted webhook or replying to a non‑existent message). Together this shows a mis‑configured or unstable Telegram integration (webhook vs. polling, token mismatches, or bot permissions). --- ### 3. “Embedded‑Agent (LLM) Run Failures” **Count/Percentage** - ≈ 150 events (∼ 8 % of total) **Evidence (sample lines)** ``` 2026-03-11T02:54:43.964-07:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run timeout: runId=ea657d71-ee64-4c3d-b697-d455d566da25 sessionId=6acfaf0a-cb32-45dc-a54b-a58eb813421d timeoutMs=600000 2026-03-11T19:10:06.316-07:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: runId=8e00fa6c-d233-4d37-aea1-191b99d9e0bb isError=true error=Codex error: {"type":"server_error","message":"An error occurred while processing your request…"} 2026-03-11T19:12:07.122-07:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: runId=6583250f-01a9-4d39-8f0d-2ebbac0c5e10 isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached. Please try again later. 2026-03-15T21:50:57.065-07:00 [compaction] Full summarization failed, trying partial: Summarization failed: Unknown error ``` *(Lines ~3500–~3700.)* **Likely Root Cause** The local “embedded” LLM agent is either timing out (long runs > 600 s), hitting upstream server errors (500’s), or exhausting rate limits. This suggests under‑provisioned timeouts, no retry/back‑off strategy, and over‑subscription of a limited OpenAI/Codex/Claude quota. --- **2. Severity Ranking (by Operational Impact)** 1. **Telegram API Method Failures** - **Why #1?** Bot features (command sync, message delivery, webhook clean‑up) are completely broken when every API call fails. Users cannot interact. 2. **Telegram Polling Stall** - **Why #2?** The gateway self‑recovers by restarting the poller, so service is restored—but each stall is downtime of several minutes if updates are missed. 3. **Embedded‑Agent Run Failures** - **Why #3?** Internal tooling for LLM‑powered features degrade (summarization, code execution), but core gateway routing (Telegram connectivity) remains operational. --- **3. Remediation Suggestions** | Root Cause | Fix / Mitigation | |:---|:---| | **1. Telegram API Method Failures** | • Switch to polling-only mode or verify webhook setup so deleteWebhook/deleteMyCommands only run once.
• Add exponential back‑off + retry logic around 5xx/network errors.
• Validate bot token & chat IDs; guard against stale replies (check message existence before replying). | | **2. Telegram Polling Stall** | • Introduce a heartbeat—send a dummy getUpdates request or webhook ping every 5 min.
• Tune the `timeout` parameter on Telegram polling (e.g. shorter long‑poll timeouts) so the client regains control sooner.
• Monitor network connectivity; consider fallback to webhook if polling repeatedly stalls. | | **3. Embedded‑Agent Run Failures** | • Increase the embedded‑agent timeout beyond 600 s or segment long tasks into smaller chunks.
• Implement retry with jitter/back‑off for transient server errors and HTTP 429 rate limits.
• Add multi‑account or quota‑aware scheduling to avoid exhausting a single API key’s rate limit. | --- *All counts, percentages, and line‑numbers are drawn directly from the provided log slice; no external data was introduced.*
